text: Mechanism design must distinguish relationship retention from stake captivity: an in-place sanction changes which premium enters the constraint, while a pending-claim freeze moves a case from leaky to captive treatment without converting exit misconduct into in-place misconduct.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Refundable Stake Does Not Expand Deterrent Capacity in Long-Lived Delegation: Collateral, Premia, and Pseudonymous Markets (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7322599

isBasedOn.name: Refundable Stake Does Not Expand Deterrent Capacity in Long-Lived Delegation: Collateral, Premia, and Pseudonymous Markets

abstract: Third, distinguish relationship retention from stake captivity: an in-place sanction changes which premium enters the constraint, while a pending-claim freeze can prevent release and move a case from leaky to captive treatment without itself converting exit misconduct into in-place misconduct.
